solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Supply with load of seafood after initial feline cry

indicators.note: the haul is taken after its initial letter has gone

parts.note: to cater is to supply food
w is the standard abbreviation of with
a fishing boat's haul is its load of catch

explanation.surface: A caterer stocks up with a boatload of seafood while the cat yowls for its share.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes "feline cry" look like a stray afterthought, but it is the definition; the rest is a caterer's delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: To caterwaul is to make the howling cry of a cat on heat.

clue.text: Reserved day in carvery, needing filling

indicators.note: carvery wants its filling, so only its outer letters C and Y remain

parts.note: day as in 'in my day', an era or age

explanation.surface: A table is reserved for the day at a carvery, where people come to fill up.
explanation.walkthrough: "Needing filling" sounds like a hungry diner but instructs you to empty the word. "Day" for AGE is the sense of 'in Victoria's day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cagey is reserved and unwilling to give information away.

clue.text: Mean business to discuss over Christmas dinner?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for speaking frankly and getting down to business
read literally: chat about the roast bird on the table

explanation.surface: Family members get serious about business matters over the Christmas turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, literal reading: turkey is the traditional British Christmas dinner, so discussing it is talking turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk turkey is to discuss something frankly and seriously, that is to mean business.

clue.text: Light changing pre-alarm

indicators.note: the letters of PRE-ALARM change places

explanation.surface: A traffic light turns amber just before the alarm goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: "Light changing" reads as traffic lights, but the light is the definition and "changing" works on the made-up word "pre-alarm".
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a vehicle's rear lamp is one kind of light.

clue.text: Chicken shop offering to support area that's daunting

parts.note: a is the abbreviation of area
a chicken wing, as sold in a fried chicken shop

explanation.surface: A fried chicken shop's menu offers something to back up a daunting district.
explanation.walkthrough: "Chicken" suggests cowardice, which suits "daunting", but here it is just the bird on a takeaway menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awing fills you with awe, so it is daunting.

clue.text: Largely garish island spoiled Asian state

indicators.note: most of LOUD, with its last letter dropped
ASIAN is spoiled, its letters jumbled

parts.note: garish = LOUD, largely = without its last letter
I is the abbreviation of island

explanation.surface: A loud, tacky island has ruined some Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: "Asian state" looks like the definition; the state is American, and "Asian" is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: one of the fifty US states, on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Bloke in film, say, broken by female villain

parts.note: a man appearing in a film is a male actor
f is the abbreviation of female

explanation.surface: A film's leading man is thwarted by a female baddie.
explanation.walkthrough: "Female villain" reads as one phrase, a villainess; split it, because "female" gives only the F.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Latin for evil-doer: a criminal or wrongdoer.

clue.text: Intellectual dug up for broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is as heard

parts.note: dug up = mined, which is then said aloud

explanation.surface: An academic's dug-up findings are going out on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: "Intellectual" is a noun here, a great thinker, as in 'one of the finest minds of the age'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mind can mean a person of great intellect, an intellectual.

clue.text: Young man in course of salad diet

indicators.note: the answer runs in the course of the next words

explanation.surface: A young man is on a salad diet.
explanation.walkthrough: "Course" pretends to be a course of a meal, fitting the salad; it means the answer lies along the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A laddie is a Scottish word for a boy or young man.

clue.text: Face nasty trick, playing game of team selection

indicators.note: the letters are played about with

explanation.surface: A player cops a dirty trick in a game where teams are being picked.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the English bat-and-ball game; in fantasy cricket fans pick imaginary teams of real players and score by their performances.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasy cricket is a game in which you select a team of real cricketers.

clue.text: Conservative must let me think about former slight

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, the British party
old = former, as in 'my old school'
er is the hesitation noise of someone thinking

explanation.surface: A Tory politician mulls over an old insult.
explanation.walkthrough: "Slight" is a noun, a snub, though the surface makes it read as an adjective; the Conservative is Britain's Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to give someone the cold shoulder is to snub them deliberately.

clue.text: Stove crushed by outsize fruit

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a range is a large cooking stove

explanation.surface: A kitchen stove is flattened by an enormous piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: OS = outsize is a British clothing-size label.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the citrus kind of fruit, plural to match.

clue.text: Intimacy? Friday concludes with it

explanation.surface: A week of closeness wraps up on Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: "With it" must be read as one phrase meaning trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendship is a close bond, an intimacy between people.

clue.text: Finery on girl AI rendered backwards

parts.note: re = on, about, as in memo headings

indicators.note: AI is written in reverse to give IA

parts.note: the letters as printed, then turned round

explanation.surface: A computer program draws a girl's glad rags, but gets them the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Only AI is reversed; RE and GAL go in as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are ceremonial robes and emblems, grand finery.

clue.text: Dinosaur droppings covered by current lecturer

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
guano is bird or bat droppings
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A fossil's dung is being covered by the latest university lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Don for a university teacher is Oxford and Cambridge usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur.

clue.text: Overheard priest, or beast?

indicators.note: we catch the word by ear, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: Someone half-hears and can't tell if it was a priest or an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is the joke: the two words sound the same, so the listener really can't tell.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American beast of burden.

clue.text: Fool has sprayed bronzer on himself and face of top aide

parts.note: he has fake-tanned himself, so he IS TAN
the colour a spray of bronzer leaves

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, its first letter

explanation.surface: An idiot fake-tans himself and the face of his boss's aide as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The long middle phrase is a description to be restated: someone who has sprayed on bronzer IS TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a helper who works under someone.

clue.text: Eg Byzantine ploy to import historian

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricately tangled, so PLOY TO is mixed up

explanation.surface: An example of a devious Byzantine scheme to bring in a historian.
explanation.walkthrough: "Import" is a noun meaning significance, not a verb about bringing things in.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a scholar of ancient Egypt is one kind of historian.

clue.text: Living stats revised when temperature's taken?

definitions.text: Living stats revised when temperature's taken?

indicators.note: the letters of LIVING STATS are reworked
T, for temperature, is taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: A nurse updates a patient's life statistics after taking their temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a nurse's chart: the life statistics updated each time a temperature is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The &lit reads straight: pulse, breathing and temperature are the stats of a living body, revised at each check.

clue.text: You might say, more shallow-ish sweet talk?

parts.note: surface padding: owns up that the word is made up
flat = shallow, so more shallow = flatter
the suffix -y means -ish, as in yellowy

explanation.surface: Someone playfully coins a word for being a bit more superficial.
explanation.walkthrough: "You might say" owns up that FLATTER-Y is a made-up word: flatter, plus -y for 'somewhat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: insincere praise, the coaxing kind of talk.

clue.text: As some workloads are divvied, zone out?

definitions.meaning: work is divided up by department
split in two: leave, but only in your head

explanation.surface: Staff drift off in a daydream while work is being handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical second reading: to zone out is to depart mentally.
explanation.definitionFit: Work shared out departmentally is divided among the departments.

clue.text: Ranks here groan, shattered after constant training

indicators.note: GROAN is broken into pieces and rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers in the ranks groan, worn out by endless drills.
explanation.walkthrough: "Ranks" suggests soldiers, but a pipe organ's pipes are arranged in ranks, so it is where ranks are found.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe organ houses its pipes in rows called ranks.

clue.text: Fisherman's gear snags vessel at the bottom

parts.note: a Thermos is a vacuum flask

explanation.surface: An angler's net catches a boat on the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: "Vessel" wants to be a boat; it is a container for drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means lowest, right at the bottom.

clue.text: Run-down horse's knocked over sibling

indicators.note: PONY'S is tipped over, reading backwards

explanation.surface: A worn-out horse knocks over a brother or sister.
explanation.walkthrough: "Run-down" looks like an adjective for the tired horse; it is the noun rundown, a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A synopsis is a rundown, a brief summary.

clue.text: One on staff conserving nation's art style

parts.note: a minim is a note written on a musical staff
Mali's, the African nation with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A staff member protects a country's national art style.
explanation.walkthrough: "Staff" suggests employees; it is the five-line stave of music. A minim is the British name for a half note.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimalism is a style of art stripped to the simplest forms.

clue.text: Mark margins of hefty Polish edition

indicators.note: the margins are the edges, so take each word's first and last letters

explanation.surface: A proofreader marks up the margins of a weighty Polish edition.
explanation.walkthrough: Margins, marks and editions all belong to proofreading, which hides the fact that each word only lends its two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the short dash joining words is one punctuation mark.

clue.text: Increasingly sneaky way to secure duck, one sheltered by female

parts.note: a teal is a small duck
her = a female, as a pronoun
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sly way to trap a duck while a woman shelters one.
explanation.walkthrough: "Duck" could be a verb, to dodge, which suits sneakiness; it is the bird. "Increasingly" asks for the comparative -ER form.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthier means more sneaky, the comparative matching "increasingly".

clue.text: Stars essentially disliked supporter

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, its middle letters

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Celebrities are basically unpopular with a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stars" suggests celebrities and "supporter" a fan; neither is meant that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a constellation (and zodiac sign), which is a group of stars.

clue.text: Purveyor possibly managing stingy customers?

parts.note: the surface: a shopkeeper who sells things and handles the clientele
meant: 'customers' in the old sense of fellows, and stingy as in having stings, so bees

explanation.surface: A trader tries to deal with mean, penny-pinching shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stingy" is the pun: not mean with money but armed with stings; a beekeeper purveys honey and manages the bees.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper manages stinging bees and may sell their honey.

clue.text: Cut up fish and immediately start to ice on casting site

parts.note: the ling is a sea fish
stat is medical shorthand for immediately

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of ice is used

explanation.surface: A cook slices fish and ices it at once where it was caught by casting.
explanation.walkthrough: "Casting" suggests fishing, matching the fish; the casting is of votes.
explanation.definitionFit: A polling station is the site where votes are cast.

clue.text: Kitty Olympics venue

definitions.meaning: where Olympic swimming races are held

explanation.surface: A cat turns up at the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: "Kitty" pretends to be a cat or a name; it is a pot of money everyone chips into.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool is a common fund, like a kitty, and also a swimming pool.

clue.text: Record cached in tribute somewhere online

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A saved recording pays tribute somewhere on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cached" belongs to web browsing, which fits the definition, but here it just means hidden inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A home page is a website's main page, a place online.

clue.text: Comment on endless trouble at gallery

indicators.note: ANNOY loses its last letter

parts.note: the Tate is a group of London art galleries

explanation.surface: A critic remarks on the constant trouble at an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the London art gallery; "at" simply places it next to ANNO.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to add explanatory notes to a text.

clue.text: Popular setter keeps fifth of puzzle harsh

indicators.note: to keep is to hold on to, so the setter holds the puzzle's letter inside itself
the fifth letter of puzzle

explanation.surface: A well-liked crossword setter keeps one part of the puzzle tough.
explanation.walkthrough: "Setter" wants to be the crossword compiler; it is something that sets hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement means harsh, usually of weather.

clue.text: Emergency response to burning eggs, endorsed liberally

indicators.note: the letters are taken freely, not in their given order

explanation.surface: Burnt eggs meet a generous, approving response from the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: A Green Goddess was a British army fire engine, brought out in emergencies such as firefighters' strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Green Goddesses were emergency fire engines, the response to a fire.

clue.text: Sauce's turned mostly full and sweet

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the sauce's letters read backwards
PLUMP without its last letter

parts.note: ragu's: ragu is an Italian meat sauce
full = plump, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A sauce has gone off, almost rich and sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: "Full" is plump as in a full figure, not full of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a sugared candy, one kind of sweet (British for a piece of confectionery).

clue.text: Cutter was capsized under first couple of scones and bun

indicators.note: WAS is turned over, reading upwards
in a down clue, under means the cutter's word goes beneath the rest
the first two letters of scones

parts.note: the word as printed, then turned over

explanation.surface: A baker's knife was knocked over beneath a plate of scones and buns.
explanation.walkthrough: A scone is a small British baked cake, served with jam and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A scroll saw is a fine saw for cutting curves.

clue.text: One obstinate horse (as it were), we hear?

indicators.note: the answer is how the phrase sounds

parts.note: a horse is one who says neigh

explanation.surface: A stubborn horse, so to speak, is heard objecting.
explanation.walkthrough: "As it were" admits the stretch: a horse is not literally a neigh-sayer, but it does say neigh.
explanation.definitionFit: A naysayer is someone who stubbornly says no.

clue.text: OK by you, I understand

parts.note: ah! is what you say when something dawns

explanation.surface: Someone checks that a plan is fine with you.
explanation.walkthrough: "OK by you" reads as one phrase; split after OK, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, informal: a casual word of agreement.

clue.text: Pronoun change fairly regularly taken in family

indicators.note: take every other letter of fairly

explanation.surface: Someone updates their pronouns, a move that is fairly common in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fairly regularly" looks like an adverb meaning often; split it into fodder and instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary trait is passed on and taken on within a family.

clue.text: Singular in style, given national team jersey with frosted tips?

parts.note: a player picked for their country is capped

explanation.surface: A stylish player, newly picked for their country, turns up with frosted hair tips.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a player selected for the national team is 'capped', after the cap once awarded; frosted tips sound like hair but are snowy mountain peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowcapped mountain has frosted tips, its peaks white with snow.

clue.text: Rebel incorporating new hair product

parts.note: to rise up is to rebel

explanation.surface: A rebel goes in for a new hair product.
explanation.walkthrough: A rinse is a temporary hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a hair tint washed through the hair.

clue.text: In hearing, recognises extremely tall story close behind others

indicators.note: each word is spelt as it is heard, not as it is written

parts.note: extremely = too, as in too kind
a tall story is a tall tale

explanation.surface: A listener spots an exaggerated story straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: Three sound-alikes in a row; "tall story" gives TALE, the tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic nose to tail is packed closely, each car just behind the one in front.

clue.text: Leave behind darn scent that's spreading

indicators.note: the letters spread out and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone flees a wretched smell that is spreading through the room.
explanation.walkthrough: "Darn" is a mild curse word here, not sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rise above and go beyond something.

clue.text: Bird back to jeer guy holding rifle

parts.note: the snipe is a wading bird

indicators.note: the back of jeer, its last letter

explanation.surface: A man with a gun jeers at a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: "Back" sounds like a reversal signal, but here it just picks the last letter of jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a hidden marksman who shoots with a rifle.

clue.text: Plant articles framing drug-smuggling mistress

indicators.note: the two A's frame the rest

parts.note: two indefinite articles, a and a

indicators.note: a smuggler carries goods hidden on the person, so the mistress carries the drug inside

explanation.surface: A plant: newspapers are stitching up a drug-smuggling mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: "Plant" hints at framed evidence and "articles" at newspaper stories; both are something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a succulent grown for its soothing gel, one kind of plant.

clue.text: Desperate when minimal understanding vanishes in seconds

indicators.note: the second letter of each word vanishes

parts.note: LEAST loses E and GRASP loses R

explanation.surface: Panic sets in when a flicker of comprehension disappears in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: "In seconds" means 'very quickly' on the surface, but here it points at the second letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-gasp effort is a desperate one made at the final moment.

clue.text: Wife tucked into large portion of eg lamb wrap

indicators.note: to tuck something into is to slip it inside, so the wife goes within the lamb joint

parts.note: a saddle of lamb is a large joint of the back

explanation.surface: A wife tucks into a big helping of lamb wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: "Tucked into" pretends to be eating; it means inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to wrap snugly, as a baby is wrapped in cloth.

clue.text: Mallards and owl sit, performing Disney song

indicators.note: the letters perform, moving into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ducks and an owl settle down to sing a Disney number.
explanation.walkthrough: The "and" joins the two lots of fodder and is not itself fodder; Disney's cartoon animals make the singing birds plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the theme-park ride's tune, one of Disney's best-known songs.

clue.text: Derriere of American I see rising outside bath

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom up, so the joined chunks reverse

parts.note: butt is American slang for bottom

explanation.surface: An American's backside rises out of the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: "Outside" describes the scene rather than the mechanism: the tub is outdoors. The reversal puts OH at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a heated bath, often outdoors.

clue.text: I'm in bed, still with opposite sex's clothes on

parts.note: a still is a photo, a snap
drag is clothing of the opposite sex

explanation.surface: Someone lies in bed, still wearing clothes of the opposite sex.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bed" is a flower bed, and the flower speaks for itself as "I'm".
explanation.definitionFit: A snapdragon is a garden flower that grows in a bed.

clue.text: A gentle heavyweight, judicious on the counter, quite frequently

indicators.note: counter means against the flow

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight; reversed NOT

explanation.surface: A gentle giant behaves sensibly at the shop counter most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal takes TON SANE together, so SANE's letters come first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As often as not means frequently, about half the time or more.

clue.text: Classical trio, big closers for the Proms

indicators.note: the closing letters of the and Proms

explanation.surface: A classical music trio plays grand finales at the Proms.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are London's summer season of classical concerts; "Classical" here means ancient Greek myth, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fates were the three goddesses of destiny in classical myth.

clue.text: Crossword-obsessed, perhaps out of inner dysfunction

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the next words

explanation.surface: A crossword addiction may come from some deep inner problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The "perhaps" marks crossword obsession as one example of being nerdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by "perhaps": crossword obsession is one form of geekiness.

clue.text: Kebab nearly

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the Turkish kebab of meat sliced from a turning spit

explanation.surface: A kebab that is nearly cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with the answer after it: "Kebab nearly DONE" is both the instruction and the scene, a doner kebab that is nearly done.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab nearly done is DONE with its last letter missing; done also means cooked.

clue.text: Club make slow progress on wickets

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another follows it, so the progress comes after the wickets

parts.note: w = wickets on a cricket scorecard
to edge forward is to inch along

explanation.surface: A cricket club edges slowly towards taking wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: "Club" wants to be a sports club; it is a golf club, the wedge.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf club with a steeply angled face.

clue.text: Retiring rambler enters cool motor event

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the rambler goes between the race's two letters

parts.note: the TT races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A shy hiker turns up at a trendy motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man. "Rambler" reads as a walker, and Rover is also a car maker, fitting the motor event.
explanation.definitionFit: Introvert is used adjectivally to mean shy and retiring.

clue.text: Always defending politician or monarch

explanation.surface: Forever taking the side of either the politician or the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: "Or" looks like it offers a choice between the definitions; it is just two letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a ruler of an empire is the highest kind of monarch.

clue.text: Each child sports fur matching the time of year

explanation.surface: Every child dresses in fur, just right for winter.
explanation.walkthrough: "Sports" means wears, but it is the fur doing the wearing: the child's letters sit inside it, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: suited to the season, like snow in winter.

clue.text: Wicked lady darts off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, like milk turning, so the letters spoil into a new order

explanation.surface: A wicked woman darts away.
explanation.walkthrough: "Darts off" reads as a verb phrase; "darts" is fodder and "off" the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with an old-fashioned melodrama ring: cruel and underhand.
